text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A lucrative narcotics trade operated by a network of well-organised drug barons is rampant, according to Daily Nation newspaper investigative reporters.

- A National Convention attended by opposition civil society groups resolves to grant immunity to the president from prosecution for any wrongdoing if he allows comprehensive constitutional reforms before general elections this year.
- At least 2,000 chicks die in flash floods in Nairobi.
- Belgium-based Kenyan professional Mike Okoth's hat trick saves the day for Kenya in world-cup qualifier, topping 4-3 against Burkina Faso.
- Two assistant ministers say government efforts to stamp out banditry in Northern Kenya will never succeed unless tribal militia are disarmed.
- 20 families spent the weekend in the cold following a heavy downpour that ripped off roofs and destroyed some homes in Nairobi.

- A controversial tour of Nyanza and Western provinces by opposition leaders Kenneth Matiba and Raila Odinga degenerates into an argument over who will be the first to land in State House and a scathing attack on ethnic Luhya leaders.
- Seven guns and 25 rounds of ammunition are recovered by police in Nairobi from suspected gangsters.
- A motorist whose car veered off the road and ploughed into a bush along the Nairobi-Nakuru highway receives assistance from President Daniel arap Moi.

- Tough prohibitions against smoking in public places, cigarette sponsorship of sporting events, tobacco advertising and cigarette sales to under-18 could take effect this year if the Tobacco Control Bill 1995 is passed by parliament.
- A team of experts will fly to Tanzania's southern Lindi region to assess the damage caused by floods which claimed 46 lives and left 2,000 people homeless.
- Dar es Salaam port authorities in Tanzania offer the Ugandan government cargo depots.
